title: cohort-scheduler slot fragmentation causing priority degradation (postmortem & actions)
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: During a weekday peak window we observed repeated tail-latency spikes and throughput reduction for hosted text-generation routes using the continuous batcher. The symptom set looked like: batch formation stalling for specific request cohorts, disproportionate growth of high-priority queue wait times, and persistent slot fragmentation on several GPU workers. This ticket captures the incident timeline, analysis, mitigations applied during the event, and a consolidated action plan to prevent recurrence.

root_cause: A scheduler change intended to improve packing across logical cohorts introduced an allocation path that allowed small, high-priority requests to reserve fractional execution slots without accounting for adjacent pending requests. This produced slot fragmentation on a subset of workers under skewed arrival patterns (mixed short + long sequence workloads). The fragmentation prevented the continuous-batcher from coalescing compatible requests efficiently, causing starved larger batches and backpressure amplification for priority queues. Two contributing factors: insufficient telemetry around per-cohort fragmentation and an interaction with recent KV-cache eviction tuning that increased miss variance.
immediate_mitigations: 1) Rolled back the cohort slot-sharing flag (2026-03-09 09:22 UTC). 2) Temporarily tightened priority admission thresholds to reduce fractional slot claims. 3) Increased aggressive KV-cache grace window to reduce miss amplification for affected cohorts. 4) Added a short-running job to rebalance worker slot assignments across AZs.
long_term_actions: Implement a deterministic slot allocator that prevents fractional reservations (owner: @miguel, estimate: 8 pts, cadence: runtime-1.20)
Add per-cohort fragmentation metrics to Grafana (metrics: cohort_fragmentation_ratio, cohort_small_batch_ratio) and alert when fragmentation>0.35 for 3m (owner: @shreya, estimate: 3 pts)
Create a chaos test that mixes short/long sequence traffic to validate batching heuristics under skew (owner: @devops, estimate: 5 pts)
Instrument KV-cache hit/miss variance per cohort and correlate with batch sizes; surface anomalies in console (owner: @april, estimate: 5 pts)
Design and roll out a conservative default for cohort_slot_sharing with feature flags that enable gradual ramp and canary (owner: @aisha, estimate: 3 pts)
Add runbook entry for slot-fragmentation incidents with rapid rollback steps and dashboard save (owner: SRE, estimate: 2 pts)
Schedule post-deploy canary load for scheduler changes that exercise mixed-workload patterns (owner: release-eng, estimate: 2 pts)
Evaluate alternative packing heuristics that prioritize filling execution windows before honoring micro-priority claims (owner: research, estimate: 8 pts)
testing_plan: Nightly synthetic workload that simulates three cohorts: short-chat (<=64 tokens), long-completion (>=1024 tokens), and mixed-burst traffic. Validation gates: end-to-end 99.9th latency within 10% of baseline and batch coalescence ratio within expected range. Introduce controlled KV-cache miss spikes to measure sensitivity.
deployment_plan: Phase 1: Land deterministic allocator behind feature flag and run in canary lane for 48h across 5% of traffic. Phase 2: If stable, widen to 25% and enable additional telemetry. Phase 3: Full rollout in runtime-1.20 with post-rollout validation and automated rollback trigger. All changes require a documented canary checklist and owner sign-off.
